import hmac
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import secrets
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

CACHE = Path.home() / '.cache/oma-speak'
CACHE.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True, mode=0o700)
TOKEN = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
PORT = 18763
ORIGIN = f'http://127.0.0.1:{PORT}'
PAGE_PATH = Path(__file__).with_name('index.html')
LANG_PATH = Path.home() / '.config/omalauncher/voice-ui-language'
LANGUAGES = ('en', 'zh', 'es', 'de', 'fr', 'ja', 'ko')

class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    def reply(self, code, data, kind='text/plain; charset=utf-8'):
        data = data.encode()
        self.send_response(code)
        self.send_header('Content-Type', kind)
        self.send_header('Content-Length', str(len(data)))
        self.send_header('Cache-Control', 'no-store')
        self.send_header('X-Frame-Options', 'DENY')
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(data)

    def do_GET(self):
        if self.headers.get('Host') != f'127.0.0.1:{PORT}':
            return self.reply(403, 'Invalid host')
        if self.path == '/language':
            value = LANG_PATH.read_text().strip() if LANG_PATH.exists() else ''
            return self.reply(200, value if value in LANGUAGES else LANGUAGES[0])
        if self.path == '/health':
            return self.reply(200, 'oma-speak-v1')
        if self.path != '/':
            return self.reply(404, 'Not found')
        self.reply(200, PAGE_PATH.read_text(), 'text/html; charset=utf-8')

    def do_POST(self):
        if (self.path not in ('/text', '/language') or self.headers.get('Origin') != ORIGIN
                or not hmac.compare_digest(self.headers.get('X-Speak-Token', ''), TOKEN)):
            return self.reply(403, 'Forbidden')
        try:
            size = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length', '0'))
            if not 0 < size <= 65536:
                return self.reply(413, 'Text too long')
            body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(size))
            if self.path == '/language':
                value = body.get('language')
                if value not in LANGUAGES:
                    raise ValueError()
                LANG_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                temp = LANG_PATH.with_name(LANG_PATH.name+'.tmp')
                temp.write_text(value)
                os.chmod(temp, 0o600)
                temp.replace(LANG_PATH)
                return self.reply(200, 'Language saved')
            text = body['text']
            if not isinstance(text, str) or len(text) > 16000:
                raise ValueError()
            # Keep terminal escape/control sequences out of Bash insertion.
            text = ''.join(c for c in text if c >= ' ' and c != '\x7f').strip()
            tmp = CACHE / 'latest.tmp'
            tmp.write_text(text)
            os.chmod(tmp, 0o600)
            tmp.replace(CACHE / 'latest.txt')
            self.reply(200, 'Saved. Return to the launcher and tap Send to target.')
        except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError, UnicodeError):
            self.reply(400, 'Invalid text')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(('127.0.0.1', PORT), Handler)
    server.daemon_threads = True
    tokenfile = CACHE / 'token'
    tokenfile.write_text(TOKEN)
    os.chmod(tokenfile, 0o600)
    server.serve_forever()

#!/bin/bash
# tesla-status-widget 1.4
# Read-only Tesla status for the home-screen widget.
#
# Talks to Tesla's owner API. Never calls wake_up. A parked, awake car is
# read at most once every 15 minutes, so this tile cannot be what keeps it
# from sleeping. Asleep and offline cars return the last reading.
#
# The refresh token is the whole account. It lives only in
# ~/.config/omarchy-tesla/refresh-token (mode 600), never in the widget file
# and never on a command line.

set -uo pipefail
umask 077

readonly OWNER_API="https://owner-api.teslamotors.com/api/1"
readonly OWNER_API_CN="https://owner-api.vn.cloud.tesla.cn/api/1"
readonly AUTH="https://auth.tesla.com/oauth2/v3"
readonly AUTH_CN="https://auth.tesla.cn/oauth2/v3"
readonly CLIENT_ID="ownerapi"
readonly SCOPE="openid email offline_access"
# Token calls must be TLS 1.3. Tesla records the handshake in the token and
# the owner API rejects TLS 1.2 with a message that looks like "use the Fleet
# API". The token is fine; the handshake was not.
readonly TLS_PIN="--tlsv1.3"
readonly APP_UA="Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 10; Pixel 3) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/4.0 Chrome/120.0 Mobile Safari/537.36"
readonly APP_TAG="TeslaApp/4.30.6"

CONFIG_DIR="${OMARCHY_TESLA_CONFIG_DIR:-${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/omarchy-tesla}"
CACHE_DIR="${OMARCHY_TESLA_CACHE_DIR:-${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-$HOME/.cache}/omarchy-tesla}"
readonly API_ERROR_FILE="$CACHE_DIR/.last-error"
readonly PARK_THROTTLE=900
readonly DRIVE_THROTTLE=10
readonly CHARGE_THROTTLE=45

die() { printf 'tesla-status: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

fail_json() {
  jq -cn --arg error "${1:-not signed in}" --arg hint "${2-}" \
    '{ready: false, error: $error, hint: (if $hint == "" then null else $hint end)}'
  exit 0
}

need() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "$1 is required but not installed"; }

need curl
need jq
need openssl

mkdir -p "$CONFIG_DIR" "$CACHE_DIR/cars"
# Owner-only. The refresh token for the whole account lives in this directory.
chmod 700 "$CONFIG_DIR" "$CACHE_DIR" "$CACHE_DIR/cars" 2>/dev/null || true

now() { date +%s; }

# Only plain digits reach arithmetic. A forged expires_in never becomes shell code.
number_or() {
  local value="$1" fallback="$2"
  case "$value" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) printf '%s' "$fallback"; return 0 ;;
  esac
  [ "${#value}" -le 12 ] || { printf '%s' "$fallback"; return 0; }
  printf '%s' "$((10#$value))"
}

write_private() {
  local path="$1" tmp
  tmp=$(mktemp "${path}.XXXXXX") || return 1
  cat > "$tmp" || { rm -f "$tmp"; return 1; }
  chmod 600 "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || true
  mv -f "$tmp" "$path"
}

read_first_line() {
  [ -r "$1" ] || return 1
  local line
  line=$(head -n 1 "$1" | tr -d '\r\n')
  [ -n "$line" ] || return 1
  printf '%s' "$line"
}

jwt_issuer() {
  local token="$1" payload padding
  payload=${token#*.}
  [ "$payload" != "$token" ] || return 1
  payload=${payload%%.*}
  case "$payload" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_-]*) return 1 ;; esac
  case $((${#payload} % 4)) in
    0) padding="" ;;
    2) padding="==" ;;
    3) padding="=" ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
  # Issuer claim only: a China account uses Tesla's China servers, and
  # every other account uses the global ones. This is not a downloaded payload.
  printf '%s%s' "$payload" "$padding" | tr '_-' '/+' \
    | openssl base64 -d -A 2>/dev/null \
    | jq -er '.iss | strings | select(length > 0)' 2>/dev/null
}

auth_for() {
  case "$(jwt_issuer "$1" || true)" in
    https://auth.tesla.cn/oauth2/v3) printf '%s' "$AUTH_CN" ;;
    *) printf '%s' "$AUTH" ;;
  esac
}

owner_api_for() {
  case "$(jwt_issuer "$1" || true)" in
    https://auth.tesla.cn/oauth2/v3) printf '%s' "$OWNER_API_CN" ;;
    *) printf '%s' "$OWNER_API" ;;
  esac
}

refresh_token() {
  if [ -n "${TESLA_REFRESH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then printf '%s' "$TESLA_REFRESH_TOKEN"; return 0; fi
  read_first_line "$CONFIG_DIR/refresh-token"
}

# Mint an access token. The refresh token is written on stdin, never as an
# argument, because arguments are world-readable in /proc.
mint_access_token() {
  local refresh="$1" auth response token expires_in new_refresh
  [ -n "$refresh" ] || return 1
  auth=$(auth_for "$refresh")
  response=$(
    jq -cRn --arg id "$CLIENT_ID" --arg scope "$SCOPE" \
      '{grant_type: "refresh_token", client_id: $id, refresh_token: input, scope: $scope}' \
      <<<"$refresh" |
      curl -sS $TLS_PIN -m 20 -X POST "$auth/token" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -H "User-Agent: $APP_UA" \
        -H "X-Tesla-User-Agent: $APP_TAG" \
        --data-binary @-
  ) || return 1
  token=$(printf '%s' "$response" | jq -r '.access_token // empty' 2>/dev/null) || true
  [ -n "$token" ] || return 1
  expires_in=$(number_or "$(printf '%s' "$response" | jq -r '.expires_in // empty' 2>/dev/null)" 28800)
  new_refresh=$(printf '%s' "$response" | jq -r '.refresh_token // empty' 2>/dev/null) || true
  write_private "$CONFIG_DIR/access-token" <<<"$token"
  write_private "$CONFIG_DIR/access-token-expires" <<<"$(( $(now) + expires_in ))"
  [ -n "$new_refresh" ] && write_private "$CONFIG_DIR/refresh-token" <<<"$new_refresh"
  printf '%s' "$token"
}

access_token() {
  if [ -n "${TESLA_ACCESS_TOKEN:-}" ]; then printf '%s' "$TESLA_ACCESS_TOKEN"; return 0; fi
  local token expires
  token=$(read_first_line "$CONFIG_DIR/access-token" 2>/dev/null) || token=""
  expires=$(number_or "$(read_first_line "$CONFIG_DIR/access-token-expires" 2>/dev/null || true)" 0)
  if [ -n "$token" ] && [ "$expires" -gt "$(( $(now) + 60 ))" ]; then
    printf '%s' "$token"
    return 0
  fi
  local refresh
  refresh=$(refresh_token) || return 1
  mint_access_token "$refresh"
}

api_error() { cat "$API_ERROR_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; }

api_hint() {
  case "$(api_error)" in
    "owner API retired"*) printf '%s' "this account has to use Tesla's Fleet API, which this tile does not speak" ;;
    "not signed in") printf '%s' "paste a refresh token with: tesla-status token" ;;
    *) printf '' ;;
  esac
}

# GET only. There is no method argument, so this cannot wake the car.
api_get() {
  local path="$1" token owner_api body complaint
  : > "$API_ERROR_FILE"
  token=$(access_token) || { printf 'not signed in' > "$API_ERROR_FILE"; return 2; }
  owner_api=$(owner_api_for "$token")
  case "$token" in
    *[\"\\]*|*[[:space:]]*) printf 'malformed token' > "$API_ERROR_FILE"; return 2 ;;
  esac
  case "$path" in
    *[!A-Za-z0-9_./?=%-]*) printf 'bad request' > "$API_ERROR_FILE"; return 2 ;;

  # The bearer token is a curl config on stdin, not an argument: arguments
  # are world-readable in /proc for as long as the request runs.
  body=$(
    curl -sS -m 12 -X GET --config - \
      -H "User-Agent: $APP_UA" \
      -H "X-Tesla-User-Agent: $APP_TAG" \
      -H "Accept: application/json" \
      "$owner_api/$path" <<EOF
header = "Authorization: Bearer ${token}"
EOF

  complaint=$(printf '%s' "$body" | jq -r '.error // empty' 2>/dev/null) || complaint=""

    "") ;;
    *fleet-api*|*fleetapi*) printf 'owner API retired for this account' > "$API_ERROR_FILE" ;;
    *) printf '%s' "$complaint" > "$API_ERROR_FILE" ;;
  esac
  printf '%s' "$body"

    def flag($v): ($v // 0) != 0;
    def press($v; $pc): if $v == null or $v <= 0 then null else ($v * $pc * 10 | round / 10) end;
    . as $r
    | ($r.gui_settings.gui_distance_units // "km/hr") as $units

    | (if ($units | startswith("mi")) then "mi" else "km" end) as $dist

    | (if $fahrenheit then "°F" else "°C" end) as $tunit
    | (($r.gui_settings.gui_tirepressure_units // "Bar") | ascii_downcase == "psi") as $psi
    | (if $psi then 14.5038 else 1 end) as $pc
    | (if $psi then "psi" else "bar" end) as $punit
    | press($r.vehicle_state.tpms_pressure_fl; $pc) as $fl
    | press($r.vehicle_state.tpms_pressure_fr; $pc) as $fr
    | press($r.vehicle_state.tpms_pressure_rl; $pc) as $rl
    | press($r.vehicle_state.tpms_pressure_rr; $pc) as $rr
    | ([$fl, $fr, $rl, $rr] | map(select(. != null))) as $tpms
    | ([(if (flag($r.vehicle_state.df) or flag($r.vehicle_state.dr)
            or flag($r.vehicle_state.pf) or flag($r.vehicle_state.pr)) then "door" else empty end),
        (if flag($r.vehicle_state.ft) then "frunk" else empty end),
        (if flag($r.vehicle_state.rt) then "trunk" else empty end),
        (if (flag($r.vehicle_state.fd_window) or flag($r.vehicle_state.fp_window)
            or flag($r.vehicle_state.rd_window) or flag($r.vehicle_state.rp_window)) then "window" else empty end)]) as $open
    | {
        name: (if ($r.vehicle_state.vehicle_name // "") == "" then
                 (if $fallback == "" then "Tesla" else $fallback end)
               else $r.vehicle_state.vehicle_name end),
        vin: $r.vin,
        car_type: ({"model3":"model 3","modely":"model y","models":"model s","modelx":"model x",
                    "cybertruck":"cybertruck","semi":"semi"}[$r.vehicle_config.car_type]
                   // $r.vehicle_config.car_type),
        trim: ($r.vehicle_config.trim_badging // null),
        state: $state,
        fresh: $fresh,
        at: ($at|tonumber),
        shift: ($r.drive_state.shift_state // "P"),
        driving: (($r.drive_state.shift_state // "P") != "P" and ($r.drive_state.shift_state // null) != null),
        speed: (if $r.drive_state.speed == null then null else ($r.drive_state.speed * $k | round) end),
        speed_unit: $speed,
        destination: (($r.drive_state.active_route_destination // "") | if . == "" then null else . end),
        eta: (if $r.drive_state.active_route_minutes_to_arrival == null then null
              else (($at|tonumber) + ($r.drive_state.active_route_minutes_to_arrival * 60) | round) end),
        battery: $r.charge_state.battery_level,
        charge_limit: $r.charge_state.charge_limit_soc,
        charging: ($r.charge_state.charging_state // "Unknown"),
        charger_power: (if $r.charge_state.charging_state == "Charging" then $r.charge_state.charger_power else null end),
        energy_added: (if $r.charge_state.charging_state == "Charging" then
                        (if $r.charge_state.charge_energy_added == null then null
                         else ($r.charge_state.charge_energy_added * 10 | round / 10) end) else null end),
        minutes_to_full: (if $r.charge_state.charging_state == "Charging" then $r.charge_state.minutes_to_full_charge else null end),
        range: (if $range == null then null else ($range * $k * 10 | round / 10) end),
        range_unit: $dist,
        odometer: (if $r.vehicle_state.odometer == null then null else ($r.vehicle_state.odometer * $k | round) end),
        locked: $r.vehicle_state.locked,
        sentry: $r.vehicle_state.sentry_mode,
        climate_on: $r.climate_state.is_climate_on,
        inside_temp: (if $r.climate_state.inside_temp == null then null else ($r.climate_state.inside_temp * $tc + $to | round) end),
        outside_temp: (if $r.climate_state.outside_temp == null then null else ($r.climate_state.outside_temp * $tc + $to | round) end),
        temp_unit: $tunit,
        tyres: ($tpms | if length == 0 then null else {min: (min * 10 | round / 10), max: (max * 10 | round / 10)} end),
        tyre_fl: $fl,
        tyre_fr: $fr,
        tyre_rl: $rl,
        tyre_rr: $rr,
        tyre_unit: $punit,
        software: (($r.vehicle_state.car_version // "") | if . == "" then null else split(" ")[0] end),
        # car_version is the firmware. An FSD package version is not part of
        # this reading; keep a string only when one is actually present.
        performance_package: (
          ($r.vehicle_config.performance_package // null) as $p
          | if $p == null or ($p|type) != "string" then null
            elif ($p|ascii_downcase) == "" or ($p|ascii_downcase) == "base" then null
            else $p end),
        fsd: (
          [ $r.vehicle_state.fsd_version, $r.vehicle_state.autopilot_version,
            $r.vehicle_config.fsd_version, $r.vehicle_config.autopilot_version ]
          | map(if type == "string" then gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$";"") else "" end)
          | map(select(. != ""))
          | .[0] // null),
        open: $open
      }' <<<"$1"
}

cache_path_for() {
  printf '%s/cars/%s.json' "$CACHE_DIR" "$1"
}

emit() {
  local reading="$1" state="$2" fresh="$3" age="$4" note="$5" vehicles="$6" error="$7" hint="$8"
  local json
  json=$(jq -cn \
    --argjson reading "${reading:-null}" \
    --argjson vehicles "$vehicles" \
    --arg state "$state" \
    --argjson fresh "$fresh" \
    --arg atage "$age" \
    --arg note "$note" \
    --arg error "$error" \
    --arg hint "$hint" \
    '{ready: true, state: $state, fresh: $fresh,
      age: (if $atage == "" then null else ($atage|tonumber) end),
      note: (if $note == "" then null else $note end),
      error: (if $error == "" then null else $error end),
      hint: (if $hint == "" then null else $hint end),
      vehicles: $vehicles} + (if $reading == null then {} else $reading end)
    | .state = $state | .fresh = $fresh') || fail_json "bad reading"
  write_private "$CACHE_DIR/last.json" <<<"$json"
  printf '%s\n' "$json"
}

cmd_status() {
  local which="${1:-auto}" nonce="${2:-0}"
  if [ "$which" != "auto" ]; then
    case "$which" in
      *[!A-HJ-NPR-Z0-9]*) fail_json "bad vin" ;;
    esac
    [ "${#which}" -eq 17 ] || fail_json "bad vin"
  fi
  case "$nonce" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) nonce=0 ;;
  esac

  local fixture="$CONFIG_DIR/fixture.json"
  if [ -s "$fixture" ]; then
    jq -c --arg at "$(now)" '
      ($at|tonumber) as $now
      | . + {ready: true, fixture: true, fresh: true, at: $now, age: 0} | del(.ok)' "$fixture"
    return 0
  fi

  exec 9>"$CACHE_DIR/.lock"
  if ! flock -n 9; then
    if [ -s "$CACHE_DIR/last.json" ]; then
      if [ "$which" = "auto" ] || [ "$(jq -r '.vin // empty' "$CACHE_DIR/last.json")" = "$which" ]; then
        cat "$CACHE_DIR/last.json"
        return 0
      fi
    fi
    fail_json "busy" "another reading is still running"
  fi

  local force=0 prev=""
  if [ -f "$CACHE_DIR/nonce" ]; then
    prev=$(read_first_line "$CACHE_DIR/nonce" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [ "$nonce" != "0" ] && [ "$nonce" != "$prev" ]; then force=1; fi
  fi
  write_private "$CACHE_DIR/nonce" <<<"$nonce"

  if ! refresh_token >/dev/null && ! { [ -n "$(read_first_line "$CONFIG_DIR/access-token" 2>/dev/null || true)" ]; }; then
    fail_json "not signed in" "paste a refresh token with: tesla-status token"
  fi

  local vehicles vehicle
  vehicles=$(vehicle_list) || fail_json "$(api_error)" "$(api_hint)"
  [ -n "$vehicles" ] || fail_json "no cars on this account"
  vehicle=$(printf '%s' "$vehicles" | jq -c --arg vin "$which" '
    if $vin == "auto" then .[0] else (map(select(.vin == $vin)) | .[0]) end // empty') || vehicle=""
  [ -n "$vehicle" ] || fail_json "car not found" "that vin is not on this account"
  local id vin name names
  id=$(printf '%s' "$vehicle" | jq -r '.id_s // (.id|tostring)')
  case "$id" in
    ''|*[!0-9]*) fail_json "bad vehicle id" ;;
  esac
  vin=$(printf '%s' "$vehicle" | jq -r '.vin')
  name=$(printf '%s' "$vehicle" | jq -r 'if (.display_name // "") == "" then "Tesla" else .display_name end')
  names=$(printf '%s' "$vehicles" | jq -c 'map({vin, name: (if (.display_name // "") == "" then "Tesla" else .display_name end)})')

  local summary state
  summary=$(api_get "vehicles/$id") || {
    local cached=""
    [ -r "$(cache_path_for "$vin")" ] && cached=$(cat "$(cache_path_for "$vin")")
    emit "$cached" "unknown" false "" "" "$names" "$(api_error)" "$(api_hint)"
    return 0
  }
  if [ -n "$(api_error)" ]; then
    local cached=""
    [ -r "$(cache_path_for "$vin")" ] && cached=$(cat "$(cache_path_for "$vin")")
    if [ -n "$cached" ]; then
      emit "$cached" "unknown" false "" "" "$names" "$(api_error)" "$(api_hint)"
    else
      fail_json "$(api_error)" "$(api_hint)"
    fi
    return 0
  fi
  state=$(printf '%s' "$summary" | jq -r '.response.state // empty' 2>/dev/null) || state=""
  [ -n "$state" ] || state=$(printf '%s' "$vehicle" | jq -r '.state // "unknown"')

  local cache cached=""
  cache=$(cache_path_for "$vin")
  [ -r "$cache" ] && cached=$(cat "$cache")
  if [ -z "$cached" ]; then
    cached=$(jq -cn --arg name "$name" --arg vin "$vin" '{name: $name, vin: $vin}')
  fi

  local note=""
  if [ "$state" != "online" ]; then
    [ "$force" -eq 1 ] && note="not awake, so this is the last reading"
    local age=""
    if printf '%s' "$cached" | jq -e '.at' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      age=$(( $(now) - $(number_or "$(printf '%s' "$cached" | jq -r '.at // empty')" 0) ))
    fi
    emit "$cached" "$state" false "$age" "$note" "$names" "" ""
    return 0
  fi

  if [ "$force" -ne 1 ] && [ -n "$cached" ]; then
    local age driving charging throttle
    age=$(( $(now) - $(number_or "$(printf '%s' "$cached" | jq -r '.at // empty')" 0) ))
    driving=$(printf '%s' "$cached" | jq -r '.driving // false')
    charging=$(printf '%s' "$cached" | jq -r '.charging // "Unknown"')
    throttle=$PARK_THROTTLE
    [ "$charging" = "Charging" ] && throttle=$CHARGE_THROTTLE
    [ "$driving" = "true" ] && throttle=$DRIVE_THROTTLE
    if [ "$age" -lt "$throttle" ]; then
      emit "$cached" "$state" false "$age" "" "$names" "" ""
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  local response raw
  response=$(api_get "vehicles/$id/vehicle_data?endpoints=drive_state%3Bcharge_state%3Bgui_settings%3Bvehicle_state%3Bvehicle_config%3Bclimate_state") || {
    emit "$cached" "$state" false "" "" "$names" "$(api_error)" "$(api_hint)"
    return 0
  }
  raw=$(printf '%s' "$response" | jq -c '.response // empty' 2>/dev/null) || raw=""
  if [ -z "$raw" ] || ! printf '%s' "$raw" | jq -e '.charge_state and .drive_state' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    # 408, or a car that just fell asleep. Do not retry: retrying is how a
    # tile wakes a car that was on its way to sleep.
    [ "$force" -eq 1 ] && note="not awake, so this is the last reading"
    emit "$cached" "asleep" false "" "$note" "$names" "" ""
    return 0
  fi

  local reading
  reading=$(reading_json "$raw" "$state" true "$name") || fail_json "bad reading"
  write_private "$cache" <<<"$reading"
  emit "$reading" "$state" true 0 "" "$names" "" ""
}

case "${1:-status}" in
  status) shift; cmd_status "$@" ;;
  token) cmd_token ;;
  *) fail_json "unknown command" ;;
esac
TESLA_STATUS_END
  chmod 755 "$dest"
fi
which=auto
sel="$HOME/.config/omarchy-tesla/which"
line=""
if [ -f "$sel" ]; then
  line=$(head -n 1 "$sel" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r\n' || true)
fi
case "$line" in
  *[!A-HJ-NPR-Z0-9]*) which=auto ;;
  ?????????????????) which=$line ;;
  *) which=auto ;;
esac
nonce=0
force="$HOME/.cache/omarchy-tesla/force"
if [ -f "$force" ]; then
  rm -f "$force"
  nonce=$(date +%s)
fi
exec "$dest" status "$which" "$nonce"

widgets.name: widget maker
widgets.description: Describe a widget in plain words and Claude Code writes and checks it. You see what it runs before you add it to your home screen
commands:
read -r p s < ~/.cache/owlmaker/pid 2>/dev/null && [ -n "$s" ] &&
  [ "$(sed 's/.*) //' /proc/$p/stat 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f20)" = "$s" ] && r=true || r=false
# A check copy left behind by a run that was killed mid-check doesn't stay on the home screen.
[ $r = false ] && rm -f ~/.config/omalauncher/widgets/owlmaker-check.owl
printf '{"run":%s,"t":%s}' $r "$(date +%s)"

cd ~/.config/omalauncher/widgets 2>/dev/null || exit 0
for f in $(ls -t made-*.owl 2>/dev/null); do
  printf '%s|%s\n' "$f" "$(sed -n 's/^widget "\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' "$f" | head -1)"
done

mkdir -p ~/.local/share/owlmaker ~/.cache/owlmaker/pending
# 1.1 let the agent run this checker; make checks drafts itself now.
rm -f ~/.local/share/owlmaker/bin/owlmaker-check
cat > ~/.local/share/owlmaker/make.new <<'MAKE_EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# make claude: drafts the widget described in ~/.cache/owlmaker/request.txt, or a change to the
# file named in target.txt. Claude Code writes it in ~/.cache/owlmaker/work; once it compiles it
# moves to ~/.cache/owlmaker/pending, where the widget maker's full screen shows it and adds it to
# the home screen only when the user taps add.
# Progress: ~/.cache/owlmaker/status.json and step.
agent=$1
W=~/.config/omalauncher/widgets
C=~/.cache/owlmaker
P=$C/pending
K=$C/work
T=$W/owlmaker-check.owl
mkdir -p "$C/failed" "$P" "$K"
req=$(head -c 4000 "$C/request.txt")
target=$(basename -- "$(cat "$C/target.txt" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null)
started() { sed 's/.*) //' "/proc/$1/stat" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f20; }
[ -f "$C/pid" ] && read -r p s <"$C/pid"
if [ -n "$s" ] && [ "$(started "$p")" = "$s" ]; then echo "already making one" >&2; exit 1; fi
echo "$$ $(started $$)" >"$C/pid"
# The check copy in the widgets folder must never outlive the run.
trap 'rm -f "$C/pid" "$T"' EXIT
trap 'exit 1' HUP INT TERM
rm -f "$T" "$K"/*.owl

status() { # state file summary error
  jq -nc --arg state "$1" --arg req "$req" --arg file "$2" --arg summary "$3" --arg error "$4" \
    --arg agent "$agent" --arg edit "$target" --argjson t "$(date +%s)" \
    '{state:$state, req:$req, file:$file, summary:$summary, error:$error, agent:$agent, edit:$edit, t:$t}' \
    >"$C/status.tmp" && mv "$C/status.tmp" "$C/status.json"
}
step() { echo "$1" >"$C/step"; }
step "starting $agent"
status working "" "" ""
[ "$agent" = claude ] || { status failed "" "" "unknown agent: $agent"; exit 1; }

if [ -n "$target" ]; then
  name=$target
  F=$K/$name
  # A change starts from a draft of the same widget that is still waiting, if there is one.
  if [ -f "$P/$name" ]; then cp "$P/$name" "$F"
  elif [ -f "$W/$name" ]; then cp "$W/$name" "$F"
  else status failed "" "" "that widget isn't there any more"; exit 1; fi
  task="Change the widget in $F as asked: $req
Keep everything the request doesn't touch. Raise its meta version (1.0 becomes 1.1)."
else
  name=made-$(date +%m%d-%H%M%S).owl
  F=$K/$name
  task="Make a new home-screen widget: $req
Write it to exactly this file: $F"
fi
prompt="You write home-screen widgets for omalauncher, an Android launcher with Arch Linux inside.
$task

First read $W/README.md, which documents the OWL widget language, and one or two files in
$W/examples/ that are close to the request. Then write the widget and stop. You can't run
commands: when you're done, the widget is checked on the launcher and you get its errors and
PNG previews drawn with live data to fix.

Rules:
- Create or change only $F. You can't write anywhere else.
- Nothing personal in the file: no tokens, keys, names or home location. If the widget needs one,
  keep it in a persisted state that the user sets with an Input on the widget's screen { }.
- Prefer http() and file() over shell commands that fetch or read. Poll no more often than the data changes.
  Read 'time' only if the widget really animates (it redraws every frame).
- Put values into commands the way README.md says, so a value can never run as code.
- Include meta { owl: <the version it needs>; description; version: \"1.0\"; license: \"MIT\";
  category }. Declare every package its commands need in requires { pacman: [...] }. Don't install
  anything: the widget offers the install to the user.
- Use theme colour names so it follows the user's theme. Make it look good: it's on their home screen.
Don't ask questions; make sensible choices. End with one short sentence saying what the widget shows."

cd "$K"
: >"$C/agent.log"
# File tools that can only write the draft; no Bash, no web and no MCP connectors.
ask() { # prompt [session to continue]
  ENABLE_CLAUDEAI_MCP_SERVERS=false claude -p "$1" ${2:+--resume "$2"} --strict-mcp-config \
    --tools "Read,Write,Edit,Glob,Grep" \
    --allowedTools "Read Glob Grep Edit(./$name)" \
    --output-format stream-json --verbose 2>>"$C/agent.err" |
  while IFS= read -r line; do
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >>"$C/agent.log"
    t=$(jq -r 'select(.type=="assistant") | .message.content[]? | select(.type=="tool_use")
      | .name + " " + ((.input.file_path // .input.pattern // "") | tostring)' <<<"$line" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
    case "$t" in
      "Read "*README*) step "reading the OWL docs" ;;
      "Read "*.png) step "looking at the preview" ;;
      "Read "*|"Glob "*|"Grep "*) step "looking at examples" ;;
      "Write "*) step "writing the widget" ;;
      "Edit "*) step "polishing it" ;;
    esac
  done
}
# owl-check only reads the widgets folder, so the draft goes in under a fixed name for the check
# and comes out again. This loads it on the launcher once, like owl-check does for any widget.
check() {
  step "checking it on the launcher"
  cp "$F" "$T"
  owl-check "$T" >"$C/check.raw" 2>&1
  cp "$W/.preview/owlmaker-check.owl.png" "$C/preview.png" 2>/dev/null
  cp "$W/.preview/owlmaker-check.owl.screen.png" "$C/preview.screen.png" 2>/dev/null
  rm -f "$T"
  sed -e "s|$W/.preview/owlmaker-check.owl.screen.png|$C/preview.screen.png|" \
    -e "s|$W/.preview/owlmaker-check.owl.png|$C/preview.png|" -e "s|owlmaker-check.owl|$name|g" \
    "$C/check.raw" >"$C/check.txt"
  grep -q "^$name: compiles" "$C/check.txt"
}

: >"$C/agent.err"
ask "$prompt"
sid=$(jq -r 'select(.type=="system") | .session_id // empty' "$C/agent.log" 2>/dev/null | head -1)
# At most three checks: errors go back to Claude, and one compiling draft gets a look at its preview.
n=0; ok=false
while [ -f "$F" ]; do
  n=$((n + 1))
  check && ok=true || ok=false
  { $ok && [ $n -ge 2 ]; } || [ $n -ge 3 ] && break
  ask "The launcher checked $F and printed:
$(head -c 3000 "$C/check.txt")

Fix every error. Errors from a missing program that is in requires are fine. Then Read the PNG
previews it names and fix what looks wrong: cut-off or overlapping text, wasted space, unreadable
colours, a layout that doesn't fit the tile. If it all looks right, leave the file as it is.
End with one short sentence saying what the widget shows." "$sid"
done
summary=$(jq -r 'select(.type=="result") | .result // empty' "$C/agent.log" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^\s*$' | tail -1 | cut -c1-300)
[ -n "$summary" ] || summary=$(grep -v '^\s*$' "$C/agent.log" | tail -1 | cut -c1-300)

# The draft has to compile. Runtime errors are allowed: a package in requires may not be installed yet.
if [ -f "$F" ] && $ok; then
  mv -f "$F" "$P/$name"
  status done "$name" "$summary" ""
else
  err=$( [ -f "$F" ] && grep -v '^\s*$' "$C/check.txt" | sed -n 2,3p | tr '\n' ' ' || tail -c 200 "$C/agent.err")
  [ -f "$F" ] && mv "$F" "$C/failed/"
  status failed "" "$summary" "${err:-the agent wrote no widget}"
  exit 1
fi
MAKE_EOF
chmod +x ~/.local/share/owlmaker/make.new &&
  mv ~/.local/share/owlmaker/make.new ~/.local/share/owlmaker/make &&
  echo 7 > ~/.local/share/owlmaker/VERSION

[ -f "$f" ] || echo "$(( $(date +%Y) + 1 ))-01-01 new year" > "$f"
grep -v '^#' "$f" | while read -r day label; do
  t=$(date -d "$day" +%s 2>/dev/null) && echo "$t ${label:-$day}"
done
